instruments.official_title: The Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Section 358 Repeal & Savings)
The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Section 107 Repeal & Savings)

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: Specific performance was discretionary with the court under former Section 20.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Specific performance of a contract shall be enforced by the court subject to sections 11(2), 14, and 16 (mandatory).
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Transforms specific performance from an equitable discretionary remedy into the primary statutory rule.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: No special provisions existed barring injunctions in infrastructure contracts.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: No injunction shall be granted by court in a suit where granting injunction would cause impediment or delay in infrastructure projects specified in Schedule.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Prevents judicial injunctions from stalling vital national infrastructure projects.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: Broad interpretation of public policy permitted merits review under ONGC v. Saw Pipes.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Patent illegality appearing on the face of the award restricted to domestic arbitrations, excluding international commercial arbitrations, with express bar on review on merits.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Narrows grounds for challenging arbitral awards and establishes pro-arbitration enforcement regime.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: No statutory timeline existed for concluding arbitral proceedings.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Award must be made within 12 months from the date the arbitral tribunal enters upon reference (later amended to completion of pleadings in 2019).
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Introduces strict statutory deadlines to ensure speedy resolution of commercial disputes.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: IT Act 2000 lacked specific corporate compensation for sensitive personal data leaks.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Introduced corporate liability to pay compensation for failure to protect sensitive personal data or information.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Established statutory foundation for corporate data protection in India prior to DPDP Act.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: Limited network service provider exemption under original Section 79.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Comprehensive intermediary safe harbor immunity subject to due diligence and take-down compliance.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Intermediary protection calibrated with Shreya Singhal (2015) judicial reading.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: No reservation for women in the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Reserves one-third of total seats in Lok Sabha for women, effective following census delimitation.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Affirmative action ensuring 33% representation for women in Parliament.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: Indian Penal Code 1860 was the primary substantive criminal enactment.
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Repealed under Section 358(1) of BNS 2023; pending cases and offences committed prior to 01.07.2024 saved under Section 358(2).
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Transition from colonial penal code to Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

amendment_relationships.prior_text_summary: Consumer Protection Act 1986 lacked product liability and central regulator (CCPA).
amendment_relationships.amended_text_summary: Repealed by Section 107 of CPA 2019, with pending complaints saved.
amendment_relationships.statutory_rationale: Modernizes consumer rights to include e-commerce, misleading advertisements, and product liability.
